excerpts.author: manunlp
excerpts.content:
Yeah I agree. However,  on devnet 2, all columns were invalid. Here, depending on your peers, you may see column `n` valid, while an other peer (connected to nimbus) may see column `n` invalid.

I see 5 cases:

**1. Super node**
1.a. All 128 columns are valid ==> OK
1.b. > 64 columns are valid ==> Reconstruct ==> OK
1.c. < 64 columns are valid ==> Ignore the block, then, eventually rejoin the main fork if the main fork succeeded to get/reconstruct all 128 (valid) columns ==> OK

**2. Full node**
2.a All 8 columns are valid ==> OK
2.b Some columns are invalid ==> Ignore the block, then, eventually rejoin the main fork if the main fork succeeded to get/reconstruct all 8 (valid) columns ==> OK

In all cases, the network should recover IMO.
